subject: Peak ramp: 429/5xx wave during LaunchCo scheduled load test
messages:
From: Alex Ramirez <alex@launchco.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
Cc: launch-eng@example.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Load test (09:00-09:30) - sharp increase in 5xx/429s

Hi Dylan,

We started our scheduled ramp at 09:00 PDT and hit a hard failure window ~09:08-09:12. Observed by our telemetry:
- 5xx rate peaked ~12% (mostly 502/503)
- 429s peaked ~18% during the same window
- median latency doubled to ~480ms, p95 ~1.8s

Attached is a small sample of client-side traces and a few request IDs (launchco_sample_traces.log). We were following the ramp plan in v2. The traffic pattern is mostly steady concurrency increase (no aggressive retry script on our side), but some clients did their own retries.

Can you confirm whether Redwood applied any emergency throttling or circuit-breaker during that interval? We need immediate visibility — production launch is in 48 hours and this is blocking our go/no-go.

Please loop in your ops and PMs.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Ramirez
Head of Platform Engineering, LaunchCo

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com
Cc: launch-eng@example.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Load test (09:00-09:30) - sharp increase in 5xx/429s

Marissa / Rishi —

Received from LaunchCo, forwarding initial details. Key points: LaunchCo scheduled a planned ramp (we had the plan in docs) and they're now seeing significant 5xx/429s and latency spikes. Attached their sample traces and the ramp plan (launch_ramp_plan_v2.pdf).

Hypothesis to start:
- Autoscaler reaction + cold instance churn could cause elevated 5xx for a short window.
- Client-side retry patterns may have amplified load and triggered our route-level rate limiting, producing 429s.
- Possible inter-region routing flaps (they're using our us-west cluster).

Immediate asks:
1) Ops: pull per-route 5m/1m error and throttling metrics and example request IDs (Grafana link below).
2) SRE: check autoscale events, recent deploys, and any emergency circuit-breaker activations.
3) Sales/CS: confirm whether this requires exec visibility / credits if launch slips.

I'm standing by on Zoom; will gather logs.

- Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: LaunchCo SRE <sre@launchco.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Load test (09:00-09:30) - sharp increase in 5xx/429s

Hi Dylan / team,

Quick follow-up from our side after deeper trace analysis and client logs:
- We did see several client SDK instances with misconfigured backoff: initial retry t=100ms, no exponential backoff for ~20% of callers. Those clients retried aggressively at the 09:08 mark.
- Some requests hit long-tail cold-start paths (KV cache misses) which returned 503s temporarily.
- We also saw cluster-wide admission control respond with 429s once queue lengths exceeded configured thresholds.

We've paused the test at 10:00 to avoid more degradation. We need a coordinated guidance from Redwood on:
- Recommended ramp rate for the next attempt
- Any temporary allowance for burst above default per-account rate during the next ramp

Linking a short log excerpt below and our internal playbook references.

Thanks,
Alex Ramirez (on behalf of LaunchCo SRE)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com

Cc: launch-eng@example.com
Date: 2026-08-01T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: LaunchCo peak ramp caused retry amplification & admission 429s — request for temporary exception

Marissa / Sean —

Summary (executive):
- What happened: LaunchCo executed a planned ramp; client-side misconfigured retries + our admission control combined to create a retry-amplified traffic wave. Result: transient 5xx and sustained 429s for ~6 minutes at peak, impacting their launch verification.
- Impact: Customer paused their test; launch in 48 hours is at risk. Business: potential expansion/commitment tied to this launch (deal LD-2026-0042).
- Immediate mitigation we propose: allow a controlled burst window for LaunchCo in us-west cluster for the next ramp attempt (4x the default burst) and temporarily raise the per-account circuit breaker threshold for 60 minutes while we observe. Also instruct LaunchCo to apply client backoff fixes.

Risks & guardrails:
- We'll limit the exception to a single 60-minute window with strict monitoring and an abort trigger if cluster p95 CPU or queue latency exceed safe thresholds.
- We'll log and audit any traffic above normal for billing/credits review.

Request: exec sign-off for the temporary exception (authorization required for SLA/operational deviation). I recommend authorization limited to Marissa or a delegated ops lead.

Attachments: small sample traces attached.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Platform Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.example.com, legal@redwood.example.com, finance@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-01T12:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: LaunchCo peak ramp caused retry amplification & admission 429s — request for temporary exception

Thanks for the clear summary, Rishi.

We will approve a one-time, tightly scoped operational exception as follows:
- Window: next scheduled ramp attempt, one 60-minute window only.
- Allowance: up to 4x burst above LaunchCo's normal rate; we do not change global admission controls — just per-account burst allowances and a raised circuit-breaker threshold.
- Monitoring: ops must place automated abort hooks (CPU, queue latency, error rate).
- Commercial: offer LaunchCo a 10% service credit if the launch is delayed due to platform fault. Finance/Legal looped for terms.

Rishi / Ops: implement the guardrails and post the exact time window here once set. Dylan: coordinate with LaunchCo about client-side backoff fixes and a verification run.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.example.com
To: Alex Ramirez <alex@launchco.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.example.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.example.com
Date: 2026-08-01T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Load test (09:00-09:30) - next steps and post-incident actions

Alex —

Thank you and the SRE team for the rapid analysis. Per Marissa's sign-off, we have authorized a single 60-minute scoped burst window for your next verification ramp. Rishi will post the exact time and enable the abort hooks; I will coordinate the customer checklist below before we re-run:
- LaunchCo fixes: patch client SDK backoff (diff attached), reduce initial concurrent workers by 30% for first 5 minutes.
- Redwood ops: enable per-account burst allowance, raise CB threshold for 60 minutes, enable automated abort on CPU p95 > 85% or 5xx rate > 5% for 2 minutes.
- Commercial: 10% credit conditional on platform fault delaying launch; legal/finance to confirm.

Post-incident follow-ups: Rishi will lead a short postmortem and produce an action list (postmortem-draft.md). Please share any additional traces. We'll schedule a 45-minute readout this afternoon.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
